text: That is a laser. It burns. Please do not stand in it. I still have the cleaning records from the last one.
Light goes through portals the way you do, only faster, and without complaining. The receivers on the walls want light. The doors want the receivers.
A beam goes into one portal and out of the other, and leaves the way that portal faces. Move a portal and the light goes with it. The receiver it was lighting will notice.
The door is on the other side of that wall. So is the sentry. I am holding a doorway open over there. The other end is up to you.
I have installed launch pads. They are like stairs, but faster and less forgiving.
A launch pad throws whatever stands on it along the same arc, every time. It does not check what it is throwing.
Every pad has exactly one landing spot. Subjects, crates, the pad makes no distinction. Neither, frankly, do I.

Carry a portal through a reset field and it closes. Carry a cube through and it is recycled. A portal shot, however, goes straight through. Nothing stops a portal shot, except a wall I paid extra for.
The door up there is on a camera scale. It wants one camera. Not a person. Not a crate. A camera.
There is exactly one camera in this room, and it is watching the floor. If it watches you for long enough, I start you again.
Open a portal on the wall a camera hangs from, and the wall stops holding it. A fallen camera can be carried, and it goes through portals like anything else.
You weighed my camera. On a scale. I have been reduced to a unit of measurement.
Inside the pen, the panel turns gravity round for anything loose. Things that fall up keep going until something stops them. A portal counts as something. Step on the panel again and down is down.
